_comment: ngsolve hdivdiv#5 (mixed HHJ avoids locking, displacement-only forms do not). Verified 2026-08-03 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh=0.3 order=2, E=1 nu=0.3 q=1, kappa=5/6, reference 0.00406235 q L^4/D. Un-reduced displacement-only Reissner-Mindlin (H1 deflection + VectorH1 rotations) at t=1e-3, h/t=300: w_c=2.4415e+06 against reference 4.4361e+07, locking factor 18.2 (inside the documented 10-1000x band). The same code at t=1e-1, h/t=3 gives factor 0.951, so the thin-plate deficit is a discretisation artefact, not thick-plate physics. HHJ with the moment tensor in HDivDiv at the SAME t=1e-3 is within 0.093% of the reference. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets THIN_PLATE_SOLVER='hhj_mixed', so the h/t=300 plate is solved with the locking-free HHJ mixed form instead of the un-reduced displacement-only Reissner-Mindlin one -- the documented fix applied at the pathology site, same thickness and mesh; the moderate-thickness run stays displacement-only because it is a control, not the pathology. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 collapses the locking factor from 18.2 to 1.00 (centre 4.432e+07 against the 4.436e+07 reference), so it removes 'disp_only_locking_factor_in_10_1000=True', 'locking_grows_with_h_over_t=True' and 'hhj_beats_disp_only=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
